title: Granular subtoken timing and cache-credit reconciliation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Add high-fidelity subtoken-level timing and cache-credit metadata at the emission point so we can reconcile per-request cost and latency to individual subtokens, and quantify the impact of KV/prefix cache hits on end-to-end token latency and billing. This ticket implements the instrumentation surface, the metrics/log schema, and a lightweight aggregation job to produce per-model and per-customer token cost deltas for the Console UI.

Motivation: Current billing/latency dashboards operate at request or per-token-average granularity and miss important microsecond-level variation introduced by cache hits, kernel selection, and batching boundaries. We need a dataset that ties each emitted subtoken to (1) micro-timing buckets for each execution phase, (2) a cache-hit flag with credit chargeback metadata, and (3) a stable request+token index correlation id to join with traces and billing records.

Scope: instrument runtime emission points for LLaMA/Transformer variants supported in runtime-1.19, add tracing hook that attaches subtoken_index and phase_durations (ms) to spans, emit structured logs to the metrics pipeline, add a batch aggregation job (map-reduce style) that computes per-hour per-model per-customer P50/P95/P99 of subtoken_latencies and cache_hit_rate, and expose reconciliation metrics to Console and Alerts.

Non-goals: full retention of raw per-subtoken traces for >90 days (we will sample and aggregate). This ticket does not change pricing model or customer invoices; it's instrumentation for internal reconciliation and Console signal surfaces.

Implementation notes: produce two artifacts: (A) a tracing hook (runtime side) that calls tracer.add_event("subtoken.emit", attributes={"subtoken_index":int, "phase_durations_ms":stringified_array, "kv_cache": "hit|miss", "kernel_variant":string, "seq_len":int, "token_bytes":int}), and (B) a structured log line to stdout/syslog with canonical keys: request_id, model, customer_id, subtoken_index, total_emit_ms, decode_ms, kv_lookup_ms, kernel_ms, batch_wait_ms, kv_cache_hit, kv_credit_nanos. Prefer stable field names so the metrics pipeline can auto-parse.

Trade-offs considered: full fidelity (every subtoken) vs sampling. We will default to full capture for internal-prod telemetry for 30 days with 10% sampling for exported long-term metrics to reduce storage and egress cost. We considered encoding phase timings as microseconds (more precise) but chose milliseconds with 3 decimal places to simplify aggregation and dashboards.

Privacy/PII: customer_id is an opaque account id and we will not emit prompt contents or token text. We verified compatibility with existing KMS/audit controls.

Acceptance criteria: see separate field below for the checklist.

Related design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Subtoken+Timing+Design
Architecture diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/obs-subtoken-arch
Reference PR (runtime hooks): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime emits structured subtoken events for all supported models when feature flag obs.subtoken_emission=true. 2) Events contain required fields: request_id, subtoken_index, total_emit_ms, decode_ms, kv_lookup_ms, kernel_ms, batch_wait_ms, kv_cache_hit, kv_credit_nanos, kernel_variant, seq_len. 3) Metrics pipeline ingests events and produces hourly per-model/customer aggregates P50/P95/P99 for subtoken_total_emit_ms and kv_cache_hit_rate. 4) Console dashboard 'Subtoken Latency & Cache Reconciliation' shows per-model delta between raw token cost and cache-adjusted cost for sample customers. 5) End-to-end tests and a canary run (10% traffic) show <2% increase in p95 pipeline latency and storage projections accepted by infra team. 6) Documentation updated and a post-mortem runbook for metric drift created.
